The best peptides for your goal, compared honestly.

For each goal we put peptide products next to the FDA-approved alternatives and show what the evidence says, what it costs per month and how you would get it. We compare; we never sell.

What is a peptide? A short chain of amino acids. Some are approved medicines (semaglutide, bremelanotide), some are cosmetics in creams, and many are sold online with no approval and no testing. This site tells you which is which, what it costs, and what the proven alternative is.

How we rate

Every product and seller is judged on the same five criteria. We publish them so you can check our work.

Read the full method

  • Evidence

    What human studies show for the use you care about, not what a molecule does in a dish.

  • Regulatory status

    FDA approval, cosmetic or research labeling, and any FDA warning letters sent to the seller.

  • Lab testing

    Whether a third-party certificate of analysis exists and matches the batch you would receive.

  • Real price

    Price per month or per milligram, calculated the same way for every seller so the numbers compare.

  • Transparency

    Who runs the company, where it ships from, and whether paid placements are labeled.

How we make moneyWho checks our factsMistakes we fixedSources

What the labels mean

FDA approved
the FDA checked that it works and is safe for this use, and every batch is inspected. Prescription unless marked otherwise.
Cosmetic
legal to sell without approval; nobody has to prove it works. Fine on your skin, no claims beyond looks.
Not FDA approved, pharmacy-made
a licensed pharmacy mixes it for you on prescription. Legal in limited cases; no batch testing by the FDA.
Not approved
no approved product exists. Shops sell it "for research". Buying it is not a crime for you, but nobody has checked what is in the vial. We never link to these shops.
Is it safe?
only approved products have safety data from large trials. For everything else the honest answer is: unknown.
